subject: Clinical research: patient identifier classification and routing for study ingestion
messages:
From: Dr. Elena Morales <emorales@clinicrx.org>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ClinicaRx Security <security@clinicrx.org>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify handling of patient identifiers for clinical study ingestion

Hi Rachel / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We are preparing to onboard a new multi-site observational study into Redwood for NLP extraction workflows. Before we move forward we need to confirm whether the ingestion pipeline and inference layer will be considered PHI processing and what controls are available. High-level questions: 

- If researchers upload CSVs containing direct identifiers (name, MRN) + clinical notes, will those raw identifiers ever be persisted outside transient memory on your hosted API?
- Does Redwood retain full request/response payloads in logs or S3 by default? If so, what retention and redaction options exist?
- Are there options to replace identifiers at ingestion (tokenization/pseudonymization) before they reach the model?
- For our compliance team: would you consider this workflow eligible for processing on your hosted shared environment under a BAA, or do you require Dedicated/Private deployments for PHI?

We have a short schema and a diagram we can share. For now please point us to the minimal set of answers we need to include in our IRB submission. Appreciate a short reply or a tech call.

Regards,
Elena Morales, PhD
Clinical Data Lead, ClinicaRx
[Attachment: study_schema_v2.csv (csv)]

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions and the schema. Quick summary up-front: we can support clinical research data, but the recommended path for datasets containing direct identifiers is to use Dedicated or Private deployments for end-to-end isolation and KMS control. That said, we also offer guarded options on Hosted for certain limited workflows when combined with tokenization and strict log scrubbing, which can be documented in a BAA annex.

A few clarifying items so we can give prescriptive guidance:
- Can you confirm the ingestion pattern (researcher web upload vs SFTP vs API push)?
- Which fields in your schema are direct identifiers vs quasi-identifiers vs free-text notes? An annotated sample (even redacted) will help.
- Do you need model outputs to include any identifiers, or can outputs be pseudonymized?
- Expected retention for raw files and model outputs (days/weeks/months)?

Next steps I propose: 1) quick 30-min call this week (we can pull in security and engineering), 2) you send the redacted sample and the data flow diagram, 3) we provide a short ATO-style mapping and BAA checklist.

Elena — adding a technical sketch and immediate answers to the bullets below. Summary: Hosted does not persist raw request payloads to long-term S3 by default; we write configurable logs to an internal logging plane which can be configured to redact or drop data prior to persistence. However, full PHI workloads should be routed to Dedicated or Private for stronger guarantees (customer-managed KMS, private network, isolated GPU pools).

Quick answers:
- Default persistence: Transient in-memory and short-term operational logs (default retention 7 days). Persistent artifacts (request/response bodies) are stored only when customers enable request logging or long-term debugging; this is OFF by default for Hosted.
- KV cache & model state: KV cache is in-memory on the serving node and is not flushed to object storage; for Dedicated we can pin nodes and avoid multi-tenant cache flushing risks.
- Tokenization/pseudonymization: We offer pre-processing hooks in the ingestion pipeline (lambda-style transform) so you can replace direct identifiers before calling the model. We also support client-side tokenization libraries if you want to pre-process on-prem.
- Redaction/scrubbing: We support automatic PII scrubbing rules and allow customers to provide custom regex/pattern lists.
- Audit & evidence: We can provide request-level audit logs, access logs, and an evidence pack (SOC 2 report + config export) for your audit; Dedicated includes extended retention options and dedicated audit endpoints.

Recommended options:
1) Dedicated deployment with a BAA (fastest to market for PHI; Redwood provides the BAA template and we can sign once the mutual review is done).
2) Hosted + preprocessing + strict log scrubbing + contract annex (only if you can guarantee no raw persistence and you accept the narrower operational guarantees).

Next steps from our side:
- If you can share the small redacted sample and your data flow diagram we will create a concise mapping document (model: which fields flow where; controls: where tokenization/redaction happens; evidence: what logs we can export).
